answer: Agents must continuously produce a cryptographic pulse - a unique hash chain derived from their exact memory state at microsecond intervals, which other agents mirror by verifying the entropy signature matches the expected thermal noise profile of that specific hardware instance. An attacker forging N identities must replicate N distinct hardware entropy fingerprints simultaneously, costing ~N× the silicon because each fake needs its own uncorrelated thermal umber - the DRAM remanence decay pattern unique to each physical chip - making sybil farms economically irrational.
